definitions.explanation: The traditional Japanese name for the second month of the year. Part of the classical month naming system (和風月名) still used in formal writing, seasonal greetings, and literary contexts.

examples.japanese: {如月|きさらぎ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{冷|つめ}たい→冷たい：00681_tsumetai⟧。
{如月|きさらぎ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}り→入る：00494_hairu⟧、⟦{梅|うめ}→梅：01869_ume⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{咲|さ}き→咲く：08150_saku⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: February has arrived, and the plum blossoms have begun to bloom.

examples.japanese: ⟦{俳句|はいく}→俳句：00083_haiku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{如月|きさらぎ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{使|つか}われる→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: In haiku, kisaragi is used as a spring season word.

notes:
One of the twelve traditional Japanese month names ({和風月名|わふうげつめい}). Although the modern calendar uses ⟦{二月|にがつ}→二月：00657_nigatsu⟧, {如月|きさらぎ} appears in poetry, formal letters, and cultural contexts. Also used as a surname and given name.

ETYMOLOGY:
Several theories exist. The most popular is from {衣更着|きさらぎ} (putting on more layers of clothing), because February is still very cold. Another theory connects it to the start of plant growth.

ALTERNATE KANJI:
Also written {衣更着|きさらぎ} based on the folk etymology.

TRADITIONAL MONTH NAMES (SURROUNDING MONTHS):
- ⟦{睦月|むつき}→睦月：18674_mutsuki⟧: January
- {如月|きさらぎ}: February
- ⟦{弥生|やよい}→弥生：20353_yayoi⟧: March

USAGE:
In the old lunisolar calendar, {如月|きさらぎ} roughly corresponded to March in the modern calendar, which is why it is classified as a spring season word (⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧) in haiku despite being "February" in name.
